The core derivation involves constructing a layered belief graph where each claim is a node with veracity score C derived from source count S and temporal proximity T. Injury claims are modeled as binary events with stochastic transitions based on source reliability. Weather forecasts are treated as probabilistic variables with confidence weights F, affecting game outcome models. Player transfers are mapped through time-series correction flags C, updating active rosters in GSE. Failure modes include stale claims (T > 1) and secondary-source drift (F < 0.7). Dualities emerge between source consensus and temporal freshness, with temporal drift causing belief decay. The system enforces retroactive correction via C = 1 when new data contradicts prior assumptions.
